text:
alex: Heads up — getting a spike of customer tickets and SLO alerts for hosted inference. Lots of 504s and long tail latency since ~02:40 UTC. Support says some orgs are seeing upstream timeouts on /v1/chat/completions.

priya: Confirming from dashboards: p99 token latency climbed from 450ms -> ~9s for a subset of tenants. Error rate (504 + 502) jumped from 0.02% -> 1.6% starting 02:41. Impacted: several PLG customers and a couple of mid-market.

sam: Anyone touch rollout flags around 02:30? I see a change in the console for `batch-scheduler-v3` — canary 15% at 02:35.

deploy-bot: Rollout record: `batch-scheduler-v3` -> 15% at 2024-05-19T02:35:14Z by alex.

alex: That was me. We wanted to test the new scheduling path that coalesces small requests into bigger batches by holding ephemeral requests for up to 120ms. I didn't expect such a huge latency tail.

nina: I'm seeing repeated messages in the runtime worker logs about worker starvation and queueing:
```
[02:39:58] runtime: all workers busy, queue depth=512
[02:39:58] runtime: enqueue wait > 120ms for request id=xyz
[02:40:01] upstream: read timeout from backend after 30s
[02:40:01] gateway-proxy: upstream read timeout -> 504
```
Looks like the new scheduler holds requests to batch them but under certain traffic patterns it causes head-of-line blocking and queue saturation.

sam: Related note — gateway's upstream read timeout currently set to 30s. When a backend pod gets stuck in the scheduler hold, gateway surfaces 504s quickly once backlog builds.

priya: Support reports customers saw retries blow up and billing alarms triggered. Ouch. Need to coordinate credits + outreach.

support-bot: Open support ticket created: INC-7642 for customer "signal-labs". Priority P1. Assigned to support.

alex: Action suggestion: revert canary to 0% immediately, drain new-scheduler pods, roll a quick patch to cap hold-time to 50ms, and then re-canary with stricter telemetry. Thoughts?

nina: Reverting the flag is fastest. If we patch live we risk further instability. Also suggest temporarily increasing worker pool min size on runtimes to reduce queueing while we investigate.

sam: I'll flip the flag. Doing: curl -X POST https://flags.console/set -d '{"batch-scheduler-v3":0}'

deploy-bot: Rollout event: `batch-scheduler-v3` -> 0% at 2024-05-19T02:46:09Z by sam.

billing-bot: Notifying billing ops of potential overage credits for impacted tenants.

nina: After rollback, 504 rate declined within ~3 minutes. p99 down to ~550ms but a few pods still show elevated queue depth. Investigating pod-level metrics.

alex: I captured a goroutine snapshot from a flaky pod showing many goroutines stuck trying to acquire the scheduler lock and waiting on condition variables. This explains why a few pods got into long-tail slow state rather than all pods.

sam: For immediate mitigation I scaled runtime deployment by +10 pods and increased worker threads per pod on the affected ASG. That flattened backlog.

priya: Support comms: drafting message to impacted customers with apology + temporary credits. Support will also include recommended retry/backoff guidance.

alex: I'll prepare a hotfix to change hold window to 50ms and make batch-growth opportunistic (never block when queue depth > 64). Adding a guard to fallback to legacy scheduler on queue saturation. ETA ~90m for PR + canary.

nina: Post-incident followups to include:
- add synthetic probing that mimics small request bursts to catch scheduler-induced HOF blocking
- add alert when pod queue depth > 200 for >1m
- add test harness that runs scheduler under multi-tenant skewed load
- consider increasing gateway upstream read timeout in conjunction with faster degrade/fallback logic so 504s aren't churned for brief restarts

sam: Filing incident ticket with summary and owners. Tagging infrastructure and SDK teams for retry/backoff guidance.

priya: Final note — we should run a retrospective on canary risk profile: require synthetic smoke for any scheduling/batching changes and stricter rollback automation (auto kill new pods on restart storms).

support-bot: Customer comms draft ready for review in #support-drafts.

billing-bot: Billing ops queued credits for tickets opened between 02:35-03:05 UTC for affected orgs.

alex: Thanks team. I'll follow up with PR link and request to re-canary only after staging load test passes. Keep thread updated if any customers call in.

nina: Monitoring looks stable for now — will keep 24m watch. Closing the emergency loop if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
